comments.author: @stellarsoulartist
comments.text:
⚠️ People saying to use chemicals to kill bamboo are only going to make it easier for them to survive in the long run, because chemicals also kill the beneficial microorganisms in the soil that help prevent rhizomes that love poor soil conditions from spreading. The BEST advice is to starve the rhizomes like the gardener man in the video said ---> let it grow without leafing out, cut and repeat. ALSO, plant native plants with strong rhizomes to compete. 
Work on improving soil conditions with activated microorganisms (beneficial microorganisms in soil are anaerobic, so they die when exposed to air) or compost fertilizer, Fulvic Humic Acid minerals like Humic Elite PG by FoliarTech

 A person can plant a nitrogen fixer like alfalfa or clover, which when cut and left on the ground acts as 'green manure', natural fertilizer.

I used this method to get rid of scentless chamomile on 1.4 acres of land. Scentless chamomile is a noxious invasive species, and I did it organically.

comments.author: @stellarsoulartist
comments.text:
That bamboo is wild!! 🤯 Rhizomes can spread through just a piece of the root system being dropped on the ground, so tilling the root systems will spread them more. ☠️ What that man said about letting it grow without letting it leaf out, is right. Let it use up the rhizome in the roots and starve it before it can photosynthesize, then you have a chance of starving them out. Another thing to do while starving them, is to plant native plants that have strong rhizomes to out comepete bamboo in the soil.  With that, you may be able to  control them. 

But I like the idea of getting a backyard panda most! 🐼😂

comments.author: @sheenavetter8082
comments.text: I grow bamboo in my yard it can be controlled. Once you have it in your yard, you have to find where it is coming from. And how to do this is start where the shoot is coming up and start dgging there only 3 to 4 inches below the dirt surface you should find a yellow rinzone, once you find that start putting it up, it will take you to the stating point. Once you find the starting point you will need to dig and put in a barrier at least a foot in the ground and 4 to 6 inches above the ground. Concrete barrier is best. If you see the rinzone trying to come over the barrier just cut it back. Once the rinzone is cut it will stop growing from that point. The shoots start at each notch on the rinzone. I hope this helps.
